display.title: The Shpoler Zeide and the Dancing Bear
display.summary_short: How the Shpoler Zeide learned to dance from Eliyahu HaNavi: he took a Jewish prisoner's place and out-danced the cruel poritz who forced prisoners to dance in a bearskin.
display.summary_long: A story from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, told in honor of the Shpoler Zeide's yahrzeit on Vov Tishrei. Every Friday night the Shpoler Zeide would dance before his congregation with amazing speed. When his guest, Rabbi Avraham HaMalach, son of the Maggid of Mezritch, asked who taught him, he answered: Eliyahu HaNavi. Long ago, traveling to help his fellow Jews, he came to the town of a cruel poritz who threw tenants who could not pay into his dungeon. The poritz would dress a prisoner in a bearskin and challenge him to a dance; a prisoner who lost was thrown to the hungry dogs. Eliyahu HaNavi told him to save an innocent Jew. He gave the guard whiskey until he fell asleep, freed the prisoner and took his place in the cell. The next morning, chained and in the bearskin, he danced so fast that the poritz fell on his face and gave up, and he walked out free. Rabbi Avraham HaMalach replied that such dancing may be higher than his own prayers.
display.lesson: Risking yourself to save another Jew is so precious that it can rise even higher than prayer.

date.note: Aired in episode 294 (filename 294 09-22-87); the story was also told in episodes 178 and 512.
